findings.text: Public teardown interface removes sysfs presence, marks destroying state, drains pending activity, stops rescue support if present, verifies emptiness, unlinks from global list, then releases per processor and default pool queue references.

Public drain interface raises drainer count and draining indication, repeatedly flushes the queue and rechecks every pool queue for emptiness until all are empty, then lowers drainer count and clears draining indication when last drainer leaves.

Boot time parallel execution interface splits a caller described range across helpers dispatched to the default system queue plus the calling context, waits for completion, then releases transient state. Zero size returns immediately and single helper case runs directly without coordination.

Public processor mask configuration interface selects parallel or serial role by caller type, rejects unknown types, and delegates to shared validation and replacement logic under processor and instance protection.

Teardown entry points are destroy and drain. Destroy is terminal and must not be entered concurrently with normal queuing expectations; drain is reentrant through drainer counting and loops until observable emptiness across all pool queues.

Parallel framework entries are multithreaded execution for one shot jobs and mask setting plus hotplug callbacks for lifecycle. Multithreaded execution may be entered with arbitrary sizes and thread limits; mask setting requires valid role selection.

Worker creation first reserves a numeric identity, then obtains a zeroed worker for the pool node and records the identity. Non bottom half pools derive a thread name, create a kernel thread, apply priority and processor binding from pool attributes, attach to the pool, account the worker and mark idle under pool protection, then wake the thread. Any failure releases identity and memory and yields absence.

Entering idle requires that idle indication is not already set and that hash linkage is absent when list linkage is nonempty. It sets idle indication, increments idle count, timestamps recent activity, pushes onto the idle collection in last in first out order, arms the idle timer after a fixed timeout when surplus exists and no timer is pending, and warns if running count is nonzero while all workers appear idle.

Surplus determination treats an active manager as an additional idle worker, derives busy count as total minus idle, and reports surplus only when idle exceeds two and the excess scaled by a fixed ratio covers the busy count.

Attachment stabilizes disassociated status under a dedicated attach mutex. Disassociated pools mark the worker unbound; associated pools configure per processor affinity and must never be bottom half. Rescue workers have allowed processors refreshed from pool allowance, then the worker is appended to the pool worker collection and its pool linkage is set.
Allowed processor selection returns the pod mask only for non per processor pools with strict affinity enabled; otherwise it returns the general mask from pool attributes.

Worker naming distinguishes four cases in own words: rescue workers incorporate the rescue queue name with a rescue marker; per processor pools incorporate processor number and worker identity with a high priority marker when priority is negative; unbound pools incorporate pool identity and worker identity; lack of pool yields a dying marker. All share a common kernel worker prefix.

Attribute clearing sets affinity scope to a terminal out of range value, disables ordered behavior, and when strict affinity is set broadens the mask to all possible processors. Hashing and equality both consider priority, strictness, and pod mask, plus general mask only when strictness is disabled, so strict and non strict configurations compare differently.

Pool initialization establishes lock, sentinel identity values, disassociated status, progress timestamp, empty work and idle collections, empty busy index, deferrable idle timer with cull work, mayday timer, empty worker collection, fresh identity allocator, hash linkage, single reference, then allocates attributes and clears them for pool use. Attribute allocation failure is the only reported failure.

Pool queue initialization requires pointer alignment to a defined mask, zeroes storage, links pool and queue, sets flush color to negative one and reference to one, initializes inactive and bookkeeping lists, initializes release work, and initializes a cursor work whose embedded data combines the queue address with pending, queue associated, and inactive markers. The cursor must only appear on the pool work list and never be processed as normal work.

Pod mask calculation intersects pod processors with desired processors. If no wanted processor in the pod is online for workqueues, it falls back to the full desired mask. Pod type resolution honors explicit scope or a global default, returns the scoped type when valid and populated, otherwise falls back to system scope and asserts system is populated, warning when scope holds the terminal value.

Attribute commit copies new attributes under queue protection, installs per processor and default unbound pool queues while saving prior ones, and refreshes node activity limits for unbound queues. Installation links the new queue idempotently then atomically publishes it in the slot and returns the prior queue. Linking is a no operation when already linked, otherwise inherits current color from the queue and appends to the queue collection.

Multithread helper repeatedly claims a chunk from shared start and remaining size under state protection, with chunk end aligned to chunk size when enough work remains and clamped to remaining work, releases protection while invoking caller function over the claimed interval, then records completion and signals the shared completion when the final helper finishes.

Multithreaded sizing ensures at least one helper, derives helper count from size divided by larger of minimum chunk and alignment then clamped to caller maximum, and bypasses coordination for a single helper. Otherwise chunk size divides total work by helper count times a fixed load balance factor, then enforces caller minimum, at least one, and alignment rounding. Helpers are queued to the default system queue with optional NUMA aware round robin using an atomic last node; the caller also processes work on stack then waits.

Serial and reorder initialization iterate respectively over callback and parallel processor sets, linking each per processor queue to its parent and initializing list and lock plus serial work where applicable. Parallel data allocation obtains parent structure, per processor lists and queues, two processor masks intersected with online set optionally excluding an offlining processor, initializes queues, sets sequence to negative one, reference to one, and records first parallel processor.

Start sets an initialized indication; stop clears it only if set and then waits for read side grace. Single replacement allocates new parallel data, saves prior protected pointer, and publishes the new pointer. Full replacement marks reset, replaces each shell until error, waits for grace, releases old data for completed shells in reverse order, clears reset, and returns status. Validation copies online processors minus offlining processor into a scratch mask and checks intersection, setting invalid indication on failure.

Hotplug relevance checks membership in either parallel or serial masks. Online handling ignores irrelevant processors, otherwise replaces state and restarts only when both masks validate. Offline handling ignores irrelevant processors, otherwise stops when either mask would lose intersection with the offlining processor excluded, then replaces with that processor excluded. Freeing removes hotplug registration, warns if shells remain, frees masks, destroys serial and parallel queues, then frees the instance.

Worker lifecycle uses a dedicated attach mutex to keep disassociated status stable across attachment, and uses pool raw spin protection with interrupt exclusion for worker count, idle transition, and wakeup in creation and for idle collection and timer arming in idle entry.

Queue configuration requires queue mutex for commit and linking, and requires both global pool mutex and queue mutex for unbound slot installation and for pod type resolution which synchronizes access to the global default scope. Destruction and drain hold queue mutex for state changes and acquire pool raw spin protection per pool queue to test emptiness.

Parallel multithread state uses a spin lock held only while claiming work intervals and updating finished counts, released across caller function execution. Mask setting and hotplug transitions hold the instance mutex, with mask setting additionally holding processor read protection across the whole update.

Read copy update discipline protects pool queue slot publication and parallel data pointer publication, with grace waits after stop and after full replacement before releasing old objects. Destruction uses read protection while dropping base references and nulling slots after unlinking from the global list.

Worker carries numeric identity, thread handle, pool linkage, list and hash linkage for idle and busy tracking, scheduled linkage, node linkage for pool membership, flags, recent activity timestamp, and optional rescue queue linkage. Pool carries lock, identity, processor, node, flags, progress timestamp, work and idle lists, busy index, idle and mayday timers with cull work, worker list and identity allocator, hash node, reference count, attributes with priority and masks, plus worker and idle and running counts.

Queue attributes carry priority, affinity scope, strictness, ordered indication, general mask and pod mask. Hashing and comparison treat pod mask as always significant and general mask as significant only without strictness; clearing establishes terminal scope and non ordered behavior.

Pool queue carries pool and parent queue linkages, flush color and work color, reference count, inactive work list, pending and collection and mayday linkages, release work, and a cursor work with embedded queue address and state markers. Parent queue carries mutex, flags, drainer count, attributes, color, and pool queue collections including per processor and default slots.

Multithread job describes start, size, minimum chunk, alignment, maximum threads, NUMA awareness, thread function and argument. Shared job state describes owning job, chunk size, total and finished helper counts, lock, and completion. Parallel data describes parent shell, per processor reorder and serial areas, parallel and callback masks, sequence number, reference count, and current processor. Instance describes parallel and callback masks, validation mask, shell list, flags, lock, hotplug linkage, and serial and parallel queues.

Worker flags progress from preparation at allocation to idle upon creation and idle entry, with unbound marking for disassociated pools. Idle flag must not be set twice and hash linkage must be empty when entering idle from a queued position.

Pool and queue flags distinguish bottom half execution, disassociated versus per processor attachment, destroying and draining lifecycle, and unbound versus bound placement. Destroying is set once under protection before draining; draining is set by first drainer and cleared by last; unbound queues maintain extra node activity state on commit.

Parallel instance flags distinguish initialized operation, reset during replacement, and invalid masks. Mask updates stop on invalid input, copy masks, replace state, then start only when input validated. Hotplug online may restart after successful replacement; hotplug offline stops before replacement when validation predicts loss of coverage.

Creation hazards include identity allocation failure, worker allocation failure, and thread creation failure with interrupted creation reported distinctly from other thread errors. All failures must unwind identity and worker memory without attaching or accounting. Idle entry warns on double idle, unexpected hash linkage, and nonzero running count when all workers look idle.

Teardown hazards include destroying a queue with busy pool queues, which warns, dumps the offending pool queue and queue state, and aborts destruction without unlinking or releasing references. Draining may require repeated flush cycles and warns after ten attempts and periodically up to one thousand when progress stalls.

Parallel framework hazards include allocation failure at any stage of parallel data construction with ordered unwinding to absence, replacement failure halting further shells while still waiting for grace and releasing only completed predecessors, invalid mask input causing stopped operation, and freeing with remaining shells which warns. Hotplug offline validation failure stops operation before replacement.

Pool creation facts: identity and processor start at negative one, node starts as no node, disassociated is initially set, reference starts at one, idle timer is deferrable, and surplus uses an idle threshold of two with a fixed ratio and a fixed idle timeout interval.

Pool queue creation facts: pointer must satisfy a defined alignment mask, flush color starts at negative one, reference starts at one, and cursor embedded data carries pending plus queue associated plus inactive indications alongside the queue address.

Parallel framework facts: sequence starts at negative one, reference starts at one, load balance factor is four, computed chunk size is at least one and rounded to caller alignment, helper count is at least one and at most caller maximum, and unknown mask roles fail with invalid argument.
